When phenol is treated with bromine water, electrophilic bromination at the ortho and para positions gives a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol. $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH} + 3\text{Br}_2 \rightarrow 2,4,6\text{-}\text{Br}_3\text{C}_6\text{H}_2\text{OH} + 3\text{HBr}$ So $Z$ is 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Hence $Y$ and $Z$ respectively are picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol) and 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Therefore the correct option is the one listing picric acid and 2,4,6-tribromophenol. © examsnet.com

solution: Solution: Step 1: Benzamide with $\mathrm{Br_2/NaOH}$ undergoes Hofmann bromamide degradation. Step 2: This converts the $-\mathrm{CONH_2}$ group to $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ , so $X$ is aniline, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$ . Step 3: Aniline reacts with $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ and alcoholic $\mathrm{KOH}$ to form phenyl isocyanide, $\mathrm{C_6H_5NC}$ . $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2 + CHCl_3 + 3KOH(alc.) \rightarrow C_6H_5NC + 3KCl + 3H_2O}$ Step 4: This reaction is called the carbylamine reaction or Hofmann isocyanide test. Conclusion: The conversion of $X$ to $Y$ is a carbylamine reaction, so option D is correct; option A refers to the first step only. © examsnet.com
